invariants: The current Provider must be uniquely selected and identifiable as Anker AI Router before its credential is read or used.
The Anker credential is sent only to HTTPS host ai-router.anker-in.com and is never logged, notified, persisted outside CC Switch, or copied into test fixtures.
Every model submenu expansion performs a fresh catalog request; stale or bundled entries are not presented as a successful live response.

Only the unique uncommented top-level model assignment is changed in each TOML document; all other Provider JSON values, TOML values, credentials, endpoints, and Codex settings remain semantically unchanged.
The CC Switch Provider template and ~/.codex/config.toml must both contain the selected exact model id and pass post-write verification before any Codex process is terminated.
A successful configuration switch waits exactly two seconds, sends no graceful termination request, then sends SIGKILL to every running main application with bundle id com.openai.codex.
Relaunch occurs after all targeted old PIDs disappear; ESRCH is treated as already exited, while an immediate permission error stops relaunch and is reported.
Configuration or rollback failure never terminates Codex.
prohibited_results: Sending the Anker credential to HTTP, localhost, a redirected foreign host, or any host other than ai-router.anker-in.com.
Updating only the CC Switch template or only the live Codex config.
Appending a second model key, editing a commented key, or accepting ambiguous/malformed TOML.
Writing a friendly display name instead of the exact model id returned by the catalog.
Allowing image, vision, tag, or explicitly /responses-incompatible models to be selected.
Calling terminate(), issuing Command-Q, waiting for Codex to acknowledge exit, or using a graceful-exit timeout branch.
Killing or relaunching Codex after any configuration validation, write, verification, or rollback failure.
